sned.title: About SNED
sned.short: The National Company for the Studies of the Strait of Gibraltar (SNED) was created in 1980 following an agreement between Morocco and Spain for the study of a fixed link between Europe and Africa.
paragraphs: The National Company for the Studies of the Strait of Gibraltar, abbreviated as "SNED," is a joint-stock company created in 1980 following the "supplementary cooperation agreement between the Kingdom of Morocco and the Kingdom of Spain for the study of a fixed link between Europe and Africa across the Strait of Gibraltar." An additional agreement was signed in 1989 between the Kingdom of Morocco and the Kingdom of Spain for the "study of a fixed link between Europe and Africa across the Strait of Gibraltar," detailing the responsibilities of the various stakeholders in particular.

The official launch of the studies of the fixed link project across the Strait of Gibraltar was jointly decided by His Majesty Hassan II of Morocco and His Majesty Juan Carlos I of Spain in June 1979. The Royal resolution was materialized on October 24, 1980, during the signing of an Agreement between the two governments, thus creating, on the one hand, a Moroccan-Spanish Joint Committee which constitutes the governing body of the project, and on the other hand, two state-owned study companies, responsible for carrying out the work plans approved by the Joint Committee: SNED in Rabat, and the Sociedad Española de Estudios para la Comunicación Fija a través del Estrecho de Gibraltar, S.A. (SECEGSA) in Madrid.
SNED is located in Rabat (Souissi) – No. 11, Antar Ibn Chaddad Street, Avenue Mohamed VI, Km 8.

The share capital of SNED is set at the sum of TWO MILLION SEVEN HUNDRED AND FIFTY THOUSAND (2,750,000) dirhams. The Moroccan State is the majority shareholder, holding 99.9% of the capital, while 11 shares are held by various directors.
SNED is under the supervision of the Ministry of Equipment and Water.

contexte.title: Strategic Context
contexte.short: The Strait of Gibraltar is a strategic zone linking Europe and Africa, and a crossroads between the Atlantic and the Mediterranean.
paragraphs: The Strait of Gibraltar is part of a strategic zone of major importance due to its geographical position between Europe and Africa, and as a crossroads of communication routes between the Atlantic and the Mediterranean, it constitutes a decisive passage for maritime navigation.

Morocco and Spain have decided to set up a study of a fixed link across this stretch of sea, in order to consolidate their cooperation relationship and to make the Western Mediterranean a hub of vital exchanges between Europe and Africa. Once completed, this project would constitute one of the essential links of the Euro-Mediterranean transport network.

The importance of the project is undeniable for the economic and social development of the entire area concerned, as it is a possibility for integrated development. The flow of exchanges of people, goods, and services should mark the starting point of a qualitative evolution, opening the way for new territorial planning and the development of transport networks on both shores of the Strait.
In a forward-looking vision, and once the new transport infrastructures are put into operation, the riparian countries will be able to access a privileged position within the Western Mediterranean.

missions.title: Missions
missions.short: SNED's main mission is to conduct studies related to the Europe-Africa fixed link and promote the project.
paragraphs: SNED's corporate purpose is:
The execution of studies of a fixed link between Europe and Africa across the Strait of Gibraltar focused on the design, means, and modalities of its construction and operation.

The promotion of the project at the national and international level, as well as the implementation of any operations of any kind that may support its development or realization in Morocco, in Spain, or abroad;
And generally, all operations are directly or indirectly related to the above purposes.

Thus, the scope of the mission entrusted to SNED focuses on studies, design, and proposals for the promotion of the fixed link. The actual realization of this fixed link is not within SNED's scope of responsibilities.

Since its creation, SNED has continuously played its role as defined by the corporate purpose and the terms of the supplementary and additional cooperation agreements between the Kingdom of Morocco and Spain. Indeed, it has contributed to various works during the main phases of the project:
• Preliminary phase from 1980 to 1982: acquisition of basic data;

• Pre-feasibility phase, from 1982 to 1990: development of studies in five main fields, namely, the physical environment, technical studies, the socio-economic environment, legal and institutional studies, and external relations;

• Feasibility phase, from 1990 to the present: deepening of the studies initiated during the pre-feasibility phase up to the choice of a technical solution associated with a corridor and the evaluation of its relevance.

SNED has entered a new dynamic since 2017 with the objective of collecting, exploiting, and analyzing the socio-economic and commercial data of railway infrastructures in the Strait region. A three-year work plan was requested to formalize the activities to meet the ambitions of this new dynamic.

cadre.title: Institutional Framework
cadre.short: SNED is a Moroccan public limited company governed by a set of legislative and regulatory texts.
paragraphs: General legal and regulatory framework inherent to the legal status of SNED:

Reminder of the legal status of SNED; SNED is a Joint-Stock Company (SA) whose capital is divided into 27,500 shares with a nominal value of 100 Dirhams each, distributed as follows: • 27,489 shares are held by Public Bodies [1], i.e., 99.96%; • 11 shares are held by various directors.

The legal characteristics of SNED, as presented above and in the section "Presentation of SNED," correspond to the legal form "Public Subsidiary [2] with majority direct participation of the State" within the meaning of Articles 1 and 15 of Law 69-00 relating to the financial control of the State over public enterprises and other bodies, as well as Article 3 of Law No. 82-20 establishing the National Agency for the Strategic Management of State Holdings and the Monitoring of SOEs' Performance.

sned_secegsa.title: SNED and SECEGSA
sned_secegsa.short: Cooperation between SNED (Morocco) and SECEGSA (Spain) under the supervision of the Intergovernmental Joint Committee for the fixed link project.
paragraphs: • Intergovernmental Joint Committee:

This committee was created following the supplementary cooperation agreement signed in 1980 between Morocco and Spain, initiating studies for the fixed link project between Europe and Africa across the Strait of Gibraltar. It constitutes the highest governance body of the fixed link project. It provides general directives for carrying out the corporate purpose of the two state-owned companies, namely SNED and SECEGSA.
• SECEGSA:
SECEGSA is to be considered as the "twin sister" of SNED, both acting jointly in all their activities and missions.

conseil_administration.title: Board of Directors
conseil_administration.short: SNED organization and governance: Board of Directors, specialized committees, general management and operational structure by activity divisions.
paragraphs: • Board of Directors of SNED:

SNED is governed by a board of directors composed of three to twelve members, chosen among the shareholders. The Board of Directors determines the orientations of SNED's activities and ensures their implementation. It also carries out the checks and verifications it deems appropriate. Furthermore, it chooses the governance mode and appoints the Chairman, the Chief Executive Officer, and the Deputy Chief Executives.

o Audit Committee: SNED, being subject to accompanying control, must establish an audit committee. The audit committee is empowered, through audit operations, to assess the regularity of operations, the quality of the organization, the reliability and proper application of the information system, as well as the organization's performance.

Its mission is to order and carry out, at the expense of the organization, internal and external audits and evaluations it deems necessary. It may also invite any independent expert to participate in its work. The audit committee reports directly to the organization's director, detailing the results of each intervention and recommendations deemed useful for improving management and controlling the organization's economic and financial risks. This report is submitted to the board of directors or the deliberative body.

The audit committee must consist of, in addition to the State Controller, two to four members appointed by the board of directors or by the deliberative body from non-executive members or representatives specifically designated for this purpose. The SNED Board of Directors, at its meeting on June 21, 2023, decided to appoint the members of the Audit Committee (one chairman and two members).

o Governance, Nomination and Remuneration Committee: This committee ensures the application of good practices set at the level of the Governance Body and its specialized committees. Additionally, it assists the Governance Body in implementing an appropriate, incentive-based, and transparent compensation policy for SNED's executive managers and employees. The SNED Board of Directors, at its meeting on June 21, 2023, decided to appoint the members of the Governance, Nomination, and Remuneration Committee (one chairman and two members).
• Chairman and Chief Executive Officer (CEO):
The general management of SNED is assumed by its Chairman and CEO. He represents the company in its dealings with third parties and coordinates all of its activities.
o Secretariat: The secretariat is responsible for office management, communication, drafting, and organization on behalf of the General Management.
• Deputy Chief Executive Officer:

The Deputy CEO complements the general management of SNED. Regarding the company, the Deputy CEO is vested with the powers determined by the Board of Directors, upon proposal of the CEO, specifying the scope and duration. Regarding third parties, he has the same powers as the CEO.
o Registry Office: The registry office is responsible for the categorization process of incoming/outgoing mail. This may include digitized written correspondence or electronic communication.
• Technical Studies Division:

The Technical Studies Division is responsible for collecting and using site data, project engineering studies, and more generally, all activities requiring SNED's technical expertise (partnerships, events, etc.). This division consists of two departments:
o Design Department: Modeling studies of the technical solution choice (construction of a railway tunnel excavated under the seabed) for the connection across the Strait of Gibraltar.
o Physical Environment Survey Department: Studies (geological, oceanographic, seismic, and meteorological) to understand the site challenges of the future construction area.
• Project Promotion and Cooperation Division:

This division is responsible for formulating communication proposals to make the project known worldwide, develop it through cooperation with various organizations, and communicate it effectively to the public.
• Economic, Social, and Environmental Impact Studies Division:

This division is responsible for studies on the project's impacts on the different areas concerned (particularly the coastline) and, more generally, all activities requiring SNED's socioeconomic expertise (partnerships, events, etc.).
• Support Division:
The Support Division is responsible for all management activities, ensuring the smooth operation of SNED. This division consists of three departments:
o Human Resources Department: Responsible for personnel management, payroll, assignments, and travel.

o General Affairs Department: Responsible for administrative aspects regarding the management of documentary assets and archiving (including technical, legal, and financial documentation), intellectual property rights management, procurement and supply management, and inventory and fixed assets management. Additionally, the legal studies related to the fixed link project across the Strait of Gibraltar are also covered by this department.
o Accounting and Finance Department: Responsible for accounting, financial closing, budgeting and budget control, cash management, and internal and external auditing.
